hook.text: The oldest true writing appeared around 3200 BCE in Mesopotamia—wedge marks pressed into wet clay.

buildup.text: Cuneiform began as pictograms for trade—recording how many jars of grain were shipped.

discovery.text: Over centuries, the pictures became abstract wedge patterns that could represent any word or sound.

twist.text: Cuneiform was adapted for unrelated languages—Akkadian, Hittite, and Persian all used it.

climax.text: For 3,000 years, cuneiform was the dominant writing technology of the ancient Near East.

punchline.text: Accounting ledgers gave birth to literature.
